login.emailInvalid: Please enter a valid email address.
login.tooMany: Too many attempts. Please try again in a minute.
login.socialHint: Works once you have connected the provider to your account in the settings.
login.socialNotLinked: This account is not connected to FinanceAnchor yet. Sign in with email and password and connect it under Settings → Account.
login.socialFailed: Signing in with the provider did not work. Please try again.

social.title: Sign in with
social.hint: Connect an account to sign in with it in the future. No new FinanceAnchor account is created.
social.unlinkMessage: You will no longer be able to sign in with {{name}}. Email and password keep working.
social.otherUser: This account is already connected to another FinanceAnchor account.
social.failed: That did not work. Please try again.

errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

overview.addIncomeHint: Add your salary as income under fixed costs
overview.flowSummary: Split of monthly income of {{income}}: fixed costs {{fixed}}, reserve {{reserve}}, loan payments {{loans}}, savings {{saving}}, available {{free}}.
overview.noSpending: No spending this month yet. Add it under transactions.

compare.caption: {{month}}: expected and booked
compare.hint: Expected: everything entered for this month, loans including what is already booked. Booked: only what is listed under transactions. Expected “left” is what remains for other expenses.

loans.addToSee: Add your loans to see the date.
loans.stuckHint: The payment does not cover the interest. Increase it or add an extra payment.
loans.kindInstallmentHint: Fixed monthly payment, optionally with a “repaid by” target.
loans.kindDeadlineHint: No fixed payment but a deadline – e.g. a private loan due in March or “pay in 30 days”.
loans.spreadHint: Each month the required amount is planned so the debt is gone by the deadline.
loans.lumpHint: Until the due date a share is set aside each month; the full amount is paid on the due date (e.g. PayPal, Klarna or a private loan repaid in one sum).
loans.name: Name
loans.targetHint: Just a target: the app shows whether your payments are enough and how much is missing otherwise.

allocation.title: Split per month
allocation.caption: Loan budget split per month
allocation.hint: How your planned payments are split across loans month by month.
allocation.shortfallHint: Months in red: the budget does not cover all payments and deadlines there.

loans.savedHint: If you have already put money aside for the one-time payment.
loans.targetGap: Repaid in {{payoff}} – {{gap}}/month missing for your target {{month}}
loans.targetGapNoRoom: no room in your available money right now
loans.extraHint: Planned every month like the payment and suggested under “Book due items”.

advice.title: Suggestions for {{month}}
advice.availableHint: Optional. Does not change your payments – it is only used for suggestions on what you could repay additionally.
advice.overCommitted: Your planned payments ({{planned}}) exceed the available money ({{available}}) – {{missing}} is missing.
advice.free: After the planned payments ({{planned}}) {{amount}} is left. You decide whether and how to use it:
advice.adopted: Extra payment of {{amount}} per month adopted
advice.baseline: Without further extra payments: debt-free in {{month}}, {{interest}} interest.
advice.baselineStuck: Without further extra payments, debt freedom is not foreseeable.
advice.enterAvailable: Enter how much you have left for loans each month and the app shows what you could achieve.
advice.nothingFree: Your available money is used up by the planned payments.
advice.overHint: The app only suggests extra payments once money is left over. This is what the planned payments consist of:
advice.interestWhy: Highest interest first. Once a loan is repaid, the rest goes to the next one.
advice.reliefWhy: Smallest balance first, so instalments go away quickly. Once a loan is repaid, the rest goes to the next one.
advice.targetWhy: Just enough extra for {{name}} to be repaid by {{month}}.
advice.freed: Afterwards {{amount}} of instalments per month go away – that is extra money left from the following month on.
advice.adoptedMany: Suggestion adopted – extra payment set for {{n}} loan(s)
advice.from: Once adopted, the extra payment applies every month from {{month}} until you change it in the loan. Instalments that go away show up as new money left over in the following month.
advice.previewHint: This is how payments split month by month if you adopt the suggestion. “–” means the loan is repaid.

kpi.interestTotalHint: according to the plan, without suggestions
kpi.interestMonthHint: this much of the payments goes to interest

loans.saveUpHint: Off: no monthly set-aside; the full amount is only planned when it is due.
loans.noSaveUp: No set-aside – the rest is paid in full on {{date}}

due.nothing: Nothing recurring is due this month.
due.amountInvalid: Please enter an amount greater than 0.
due.dateOutsideMonth: The date must be in the same month.
due.alreadyBooked: Something was booked in the meantime. The list has been updated.
due.hint: Tick what you want to book; anything due by today can be booked. Use ✎ to adjust day and amount first.

tx.name: Name
tx.categoryHint: New names create a new category.
tx.deleteManagedText: Changes to the reserve account or loan balance are reverted and the item is open again this month.
tx.cardPaymentNote: Transfer – not an expense (purchases count individually)

categories.title: Categories
categories.renameHint: Renaming also changes the category in all existing transactions and fixed costs.
categories.moveText: “{{name}}” is used {{n}} times. Which category should these entries move to?

recurring.intro: Everything that comes back regularly. Quarterly or yearly items are spread across the months automatically.
recurring.name: Name
recurring.dueDayHint: Day of month; the last day in shorter months.
recurring.none: No items yet. Start with your salary as income and your rent.
recurring.loansHint: Loan payments live under Loans and are included in the overview automatically.
recurring.paidWithHint: Subscriptions or fees paid by credit card: the booking then counts towards the card balance and statement.

reserve.title: Reserve for non-monthly costs
reserve.explain: Every month a fixed amount goes to the reserve account (as an expense). When a quarterly, half-yearly or yearly item is due, it is booked as an expense and the same amount is transferred back from the reserve account.
reserve.belowNeed: Your reserve of {{amount}} is {{gap}} below what the items cost on average.
reserve.negative: The reserve is expected to drop to {{low}}. Link the reserve account and check its balance, or raise the monthly amount.
reserve.forecastTitle: Expected reserve balance after each month's bookings
reserve.noItems: Add an item with a quarterly, half-yearly or yearly frequency.

assets.netLabel: Net worth (accounts and investments minus loans)
assets.chartEmpty: Once you have recorded two snapshots, your history appears here.
assets.chartLabel: Net worth from {{from}} to {{to}}, latest {{value}}. Use arrow keys to inspect snapshots.
assets.lastSnapshot: Last recorded on {{date}}. Recording every two weeks works well.
assets.noSnapshot: Record snapshots regularly to build your history here.
assets.name: Name
assets.tapHint: Tap a value to update it.
assets.deleteLinked: This account is linked as reserve account; the link will be removed.
assets.none: Add your checking, savings and investment accounts.
assets.dataHint: The backup contains all your data as a JSON file. Importing replaces all current data.
assets.exportLocked: An active subscription or trial is required for backups.
assets.importText: All current data will be replaced by the backup from {{date}}. This cannot be undone.
assets.importInvalid: This file is not a valid backup.

cards.title: Credit cards
cards.hint: Enter card purchases under Transactions with “Paid with” and the purchase date. The debit from your account appears under “Book due items” and does not count as an expense.
cards.missing: Bank shows {{amount}} more – is an entry missing?
cards.tooMuch: {{amount}} more booked than billed – duplicate or wrong period?
cards.statementHint: Purchases up to and including this day go on the statement.
cards.debitHint: If it is before the closing day, the debit happens the following month (e.g. Amex on the 4th).
cards.datesInvalid: The closing date must be in the statement month, the debit after it.

import.title: Import transactions
import.intro: Load the CSV export of your bank or credit card. The file stays on your device; only what you tick is imported.
import.account: Which account does the file belong to?
import.accountHint: For a checking account, card debits are detected and not imported as expenses.
import.cardHint: Purchases are assigned to the card (“Paid with”) and count towards the card balance.

filterHint.new: Not in the app yet. Tick, check name and category, then import.
filterHint.match: Matches an existing transaction (same amount, up to 3 days apart). Ticked rows are only linked, nothing is created twice.
filterHint.card: Card debits from the checking account and payments to the card are neither expense nor income – they go via “Book due items”.

import.cardPaymentHint: Card debit – book via “Book due items”
import.noRows: No transactions found in the file.
import.missingFields: Please enter name and category for every ticked row.
import.alreadyImported: Some rows were imported in the meantime. The list has been updated.
import.manualHint: Map the columns once – the mapping is saved for this account when importing.
import.invertSign: Charges are positive in the file (flip the sign)
import.fileHintShort: CSV export from online banking. Supported banks are listed below.

support.title: Which banks are supported?

format.sparkasse: “CSV-CAMT” (V2 or V8) or “CSV-MT940” export; pending transactions are skipped
format.volksbank: CSV export (Volksbanken, Raiffeisenbanken, Sparda banks use the same format)
format.dkb: CSV export of the checking account; pending transactions are skipped
format.dkb-visa: CSV export of the DKB Visa (per documentation, not yet tested with a real file)
format.ing: CSV export (“Umsatzanzeige”), with or without balance
format.comdirect: CSV export; if the file contains checking and Visa, you choose the section
format.amex: CSV export of transactions (“activity.csv”); charges are read correctly as expenses

support.other: Automatic detection often works. Otherwise map the columns once; the mapping is saved for the account.
support.tip: Tip: for reconciliation always load a whole statement period; the app recognises rows imported twice.

import.cardSettlementHint: Payment to the card – already recorded as the debit via “Book due items”
import.learnedHint: Name and category as last time
import.dateHint: The date decides in which month the transaction counts.
import.dateHintCard: For reconciling with the card statement the bank’s booking date usually counts; purchases on the closing day can be moved to the next statement under Assets.
import.autoInverted: Almost all amounts on this card were positive – the bank lists charges as positive. The app flipped the sign; please check the amounts.
